reasons: Rule applicability is sound: Article XXI as drafted imposes only a one-way return/certification duty on Licensee and preserves all Licensor rights, with no transition assistance, data export or deletion obligation on Licensor — a genuine 'missing' deviation for a hosted software/maintenance arrangement.

The redline is a pure insertion (new subsection (c)) that leaves the original paragraph untouched — the smallest edit that reaches the playbook position, and it tracks the model language on all three elements: up to six months of assistance at then-current rates, 30-day return in a commonly used machine-readable format, and subsequent deletion with written certification.

Party direction is correct: obligations run against Licensor (counterparty) in favour of Licensee (our side), and the inline definition of 'Licensee Data' is necessary because the agreement has no equivalent defined term.
The comment accurately describes the gap and the change, cites the playbook position, and offers the 90-day fallback while preserving the 30-day export right; tone and prefix conform.

Deterministic checks both pass and the restated 'Upon expiry or termination ... for any reason' lead-in in (c) is only a minor redundancy that keeps the new subsection self-contained after the intervening survival sentence.
